If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failing test `X5455_ExtendedTimestampTest.testGettersSetters` is concerned with setting a modify Java time for a specific Zip entry. The test involves creating a `ZipLong` object with a time value calculated in seconds and setting this time value to the modify Java time of a Zip entry.

The issue reported mentions a failure under JDK 9 due to a potentially incorrect value returned from `getTime()`. The failure might be related to changes introduced in JDK-8073497.

Looking at the test snippet, it sets the modify Java time of a Zip entry using a calculated time in seconds by creating a `ZipLong` object with `timeMillis / 1000`. The failure occurs when trying to set a time that is too large for 32 bits, which triggers an `IllegalArgumentException`.

Based on this information, the probable cause of the failure could be related to an incorrect handling or calculation of time values, possibly impacted by changes in JDK 9 or a misinterpretation of time limits for 32 bits.

To further diagnose and fix this issue, it may be necessary to review how time values are calculated, set, and handled within the `ZipLong` class `ZipLong(long value)` constructor and the test method `testGettersSetters` in `X5455_ExtendedTimestampTest`.

Next, I will suggest the methods that would be the best locations to be fixed.
The methods that would be the best locations to be fixed are:
- `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipLong.ZipLong(long)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
